subject: Chemistry
name: Cambridge IGCSE (9-1) Chemistry 0971/32 Paper 3 Theory (Core) October/November 2019
description: Cambridge IGCSE (9-1) Chemistry 0971/32, Paper 3 Theory (Core), October/November 2019. Covers states of matter, biogas and organic chemistry, reaction rates and calcium carbonate, atomic structure and reactivity, halogens, compounds of nitrogen, and electrolysis.

questions.topic: States of Matter and Identification of Substances

parts.label: a
parts.question: The list gives the names of nine substances: aqueous copper(II) sulfate, aqueous potassium manganate(VII), aqueous sodium chloride, dilute hydrochloric acid, ethanol, hexene, mercury, octane, water. Each substance may be used once, more than once or not at all. State which substance is an alkane.

parts.label: b
parts.question: State which substance is used, when acidified, to test for sulfur dioxide.

parts.label: c
parts.question: State which substance turns blue litmus red.

parts.label: d
parts.question: State which substance reacts with sodium to produce only aqueous sodium hydroxide and hydrogen.

parts.label: e
parts.question: State which substance is produced by the addition of steam to ethene.

parts.label: f
parts.question: Some changes of state of mercury are shown in a diagram: solid mercury to liquid mercury (change A), and mercury gas to liquid mercury (change B). State the names of the changes of state represented by A and B.

parts.label: g
parts.question: Use the kinetic particle model to describe the motion and separation of the particles in liquid mercury and mercury gas.

questions.topic: Biogas, Organic Chemistry and Separation Techniques

parts.label: a
parts.question: Biogas is made by fermenting animal and vegetable waste. The table shows the percentage composition of the gases present in a sample of biogas. Deduce the percentage of carbon dioxide present in this sample of biogas. (Given: hydrogen 1.0%, methane 61.5%, nitrogen 8.5%, water vapour 2.2%, other substances 0.1%).

parts.label: b
parts.question: During the fermentation, carbon dioxide reacts with hydrogen to produce methane and water. Complete the chemical equation for this reaction: CO₂ + ___H₂ → CH₄ + ___H₂O.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Methane and ethane are in the same homologous series. What is meant by the term homologous series?

parts.label: d
parts.question: Draw a dot-and-cross diagram to show the electron arrangement in a molecule of methane, CH₄. Show outer shell electrons only.

parts.label: e
parts.question: Helium and hydrogen can both be used to fill balloons. Suggest one advantage of using helium rather than hydrogen to fill balloons.

parts.label: f
parts.question: The biogas fermentation mixture contains a small amount of compound C. On the structure shown, draw a circle around a functional group which reacts with aqueous bromine.

parts.label: g
parts.question: How many different types of atoms are present in compound C? (Compound C contains C, H, O, and S atoms).

parts.label: h
parts.question: Ethanol is produced by fermentation of a mixture of plant sugars. Describe how ethanol can be separated from the rest of the fermentation mixture by fractional distillation. In your answer: describe how to do the fractional distillation, and explain how ethanol is separated from the rest of the fermentation mixture using fractional distillation.

parts.label: a
parts.question: A student investigated the reaction of calcium carbonate with an excess of dilute hydrochloric acid by measuring the volume of carbon dioxide produced at 10 second intervals. The results are shown on a graph. How long did it take from the start of the experiment to collect 30 cm³ of carbon dioxide?

parts.label: b
parts.question: At which point on the graph, P, Q, R or S, was the rate of reaction fastest? Use the graph to explain your answer.

parts.label: c
parts.question: When 0.225 g of calcium carbonate is used, 54.0 cm³ of carbon dioxide is formed. Determine the mass of calcium carbonate needed to form 216 cm³ of carbon dioxide.

parts.label: d
parts.question: What effect do the following have on the rate of this reaction? Increasing the temperature of the reaction mixture (all other conditions kept the same). Using larger pieces of calcium carbonate (all other conditions kept the same).

parts.label: e
parts.question: In industry, calcium oxide is made from calcium carbonate by thermal decomposition: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂. Why is this described as thermal decomposition?

parts.label: f
parts.question: State one other use of calcium carbonate in industry.

parts.label: g
parts.question: Calcium oxide is used to treat acidic industrial waste. State the type of chemical reaction that occurs.

questions.topic: Atomic Structure and Reactivity of Metals

parts.label: a
parts.question: An isotope of calcium is written as ⁴⁰Ca₂₀. Deduce the number of protons, electrons and neutrons in this isotope of calcium.

parts.label: b
parts.question: State one industrial use of radioactive isotopes.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Draw the electronic structure of a calcium atom.

parts.label: d
parts.question: The table shows some information about the reaction of four metals with dry air at room temperature and on heating. Use this information to put the four metals (copper, iron, samarium, sodium) in order of their reactivity. Put the least reactive metal first.

parts.label: a
parts.question: The properties of some halogens are shown in the table. Complete the table to estimate: the boiling point of chlorine and the density of iodine. (Given: fluorine bp -188°C, bromine bp 59°C; chlorine density 1.56 g/cm³, bromine density 3.12 g/cm³).

parts.label: b
parts.question: Describe the trend in the melting points of the halogens down the group.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Predict the physical state of bromine at -20°C. (Bromine has melting point -7°C and boiling point 59°C).

parts.label: d
parts.question: Which one of the following is most likely to be the colour of fluorine?

parts.label: e
parts.question: Chlorine reacts with an aqueous potassium salt to form iodine and a different potassium salt. Complete the word equation for this reaction: chlorine + ______ ______ → iodine + ______ ______.

parts.label: f
parts.question: When aqueous sodium fluoride is added to chlorine, no reaction occurs. Explain, using ideas about the reactivity of the halogens, why no reaction occurs.

parts.label: g
parts.question: State one use of chlorine.

parts.label: h
parts.question: Aqueous silver nitrate is used to test for chloride ions and iodide ions. The solutions are first acidified with dilute nitric acid. Explain why dilute hydrochloric acid is not used to acidify the solutions.

parts.label: i
parts.question: Complete the table to show the expected observations when aqueous silver nitrate is added to chloride ions and iodide ions.

parts.label: j
parts.question: A compound of chlorine has the formula C₆H₄Cl₂. Complete the table to calculate the relative molecular mass of C₆H₄Cl₂. Use your Periodic Table to help you.

parts.label: a
parts.question: Aqueous ammonia is alkaline. Which one of the following pH values could be the pH of aqueous ammonia?

parts.label: b
parts.question: Ammonia has a strong smell. A beaker of aqueous ammonia was placed in front of a class of students. At first, the students at the back of the class could not smell the ammonia. After a few minutes they could smell the ammonia. Explain these observations using the kinetic particle model.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Ammonia is used in the manufacture of nitric acid. Balance the chemical equation for the first step in the process: 4NH₃ + 5O₂ → ___NO + 6H₂O.

parts.label: d
parts.question: The reaction is exothermic. What is meant by the term exothermic?

parts.label: e
parts.question: The NO produced in the first step then reacts with oxygen to produce nitrogen dioxide, NO₂: 2NO + O₂ → 2NO₂. How does this equation show that NO is oxidised?

parts.label: f
parts.question: Is nitrogen dioxide an acidic oxide or a basic oxide? Give a reason for your answer.

parts.label: g
parts.question: Oxides of nitrogen are atmospheric pollutants. State one adverse effect of oxides of nitrogen on health.

parts.label: h
parts.question: Ammonia reacts with nitric acid to form a salt which is present in many fertilisers. Name the salt formed when ammonia reacts with nitric acid.

questions.topic: Electrolysis, Salts and Properties of Metals

parts.label: a
parts.question: Concentrated hydrochloric acid is electrolysed using graphite electrodes. Name the products of this electrolysis at: the positive electrode and the negative electrode.

parts.label: b
parts.question: Suggest one observation that is made at the negative electrode during the electrolysis of concentrated hydrochloric acid.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with zinc. Complete the word equation for this reaction: zinc + hydrochloric acid → ______ + ______.

parts.label: d
parts.question: The following statements are about the procedure for making crystals of hydrated zinc sulfate from zinc and dilute sulfuric acid. Put the statements in the correct order: A Warm the mixture until no more bubbles are seen; B Add excess zinc to dilute sulfuric acid; C Warm the filtrate to the point of crystallisation; D Leave the mixture at room temperature to form more crystals; E Filter off the excess zinc; F Filter off the crystals and dry between filter papers. The first one has been done for you: B.

parts.label: e
parts.question: Zinc is a metal. Describe three physical properties which are characteristic of metals.

parts.label: f
parts.question: An alloy of zinc, copper and nickel is used to make coins. Suggest two reasons why an alloy is used to make coins and not pure copper alone.
